issues.legal_issue: A general public notice does not initiate assessment proceedings against a taxpayer who files no return, and an assessment made after the relevant financial year without an individual notice or a timely notice for escaped assessment is invalid.
material_facts: The taxpayers received or were subject to a general public notice calling for agricultural income returns but did not file the required returns.
No individual notice calling for returns was served on the taxpayers during the relevant financial years.
No notice initiating proceedings for escaped assessment was served within the prescribed period after those financial years.
Best-judgment assessments were nevertheless made, and the taxpayers challenged them.
issues.conclusion: The general notice did not itself initiate proceedings against taxpayers who filed no return. Once the relevant financial year ended without a return or an individual notice, the income was escaped assessment and could be assessed only through timely proceedings for escaped assessment. Since no such proceedings were initiated, the assessments were quashed and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 19(1)–(3), 20(4) and 30 of the Assam Agricultural Income-tax Act, a general notice inviting returns does not initiate proceedings against an individual taxpayer unless that taxpayer files a return. If no return is filed and no individual notice is served during the relevant financial year, the income is escaped assessment; it may be brought to tax only by serving a notice under section 30 within three years after the end of that financial year. Section 43(2)(a), which gives a taxpayer a right to seek assessment at a specified place upon receiving the first individual notice, supports the conclusion that publication of a general notice alone does not initiate individual proceedings. The Court applied the corresponding principles under sections 22, 23 and 34 of the Income-tax Act, relying on Commissioner of Income-tax v. Ranchhodas Karsondas, Ghanshyam Das v. Regional Assistant Commissioner of Sales Tax, and State of Assam v. Deva Prasad Barua.

rule.if: challenge_to_best_judgment_tax_assessment and general_return_notice_published and taxpayer_filed_no_return and relevant_financial_year_ended and no_individual_notice_served_during_year and no_escaped_assessment_notice_served_within_limitation

predicates.challenge_to_best_judgment_tax_assessmen: The proceeding challenges a tax assessment made on a best-judgment basis.
predicates.general_return_notice_published: The tax authority published a general notice requiring taxpayers in the relevant class to file returns.
predicates.taxpayer_filed_no_return: The taxpayer did not file a return in response to the general notice.
predicates.relevant_financial_year_ended: The financial year relevant to the assessment ended without the taxpayer filing a return or receiving an individual notice.
predicates.no_individual_notice_served_during_year: The tax authority did not serve the taxpayer with an individual notice requiring a return during the relevant financial year.
predicates.no_escaped_assessment_notice_served_with: The tax authority did not serve the taxpayer with a notice to assess escaped income within the applicable limitation period.

issues.definition: When a best-judgment assessment is challenged and the taxpayer filed no return after a general notice, received no individual notice during the relevant financial year, and received no timely notice for escaped assessment after that year ended, the assessment is invalid.
